newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks end sharply higher for 2nd day.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks end sharply higher for 2nd day.

text.p: Colombian stocks closed sharply higher for the second consecutive day on buying partly fueled by market rumors that lower interest are in the pipeline.

Medellin's IBOMED general price index rose 2.41 percent to close at 15,666.19 on an above-average trading of 2.8 billion pesos. Bogota's IBB bested the IBOMED slightly, rising 2.43 percent to end at 1,009.26 on 1.9 billion pesos.
The day's gains included heavily-traded brewer Bavaria SA, which brokers said continued to be under heavy demand from foreign funds. It rose 2.53 percent in Bogota to close at 6,480 pesos per share.

A bigger mover by far was cement manufacturer Cementos Caribe, which jumped 7.09 percent in Bogota to close at 5,495 pesos per share. Banco Industrial Colombiano (BIC), another gainer, rose 4.67 to 3,560 pesos, while cigarette maker Coltabaco closed up 4.44 percent at 3.560 pesos a share.

All were said by brokers to have benefitted from moves by local investors to diversify portfolios in the face of a likely cut in domestic interest rates, which some believe could be announced as early as next week.
"There are prevailing rumors of a rate cut by the central bank," one broker said.
Lower interest rates could help jump-start the economy, which slowed sharply last year, and take some of the premium off investment in Colombia's fixed-income market.
Other winners on Tuesday included blue-chip Banco Ganadero, whose ordinary shares closed up 4.06 percent at 307 pesos per share, and Banco de Bogota, which ended 4.13 percent higher at 6,170.
The biggest gainer among banks was Bancoquia, which jumped 7.41 percent in Medellin to close at 2,900 pesos per share. ((-- Javier Mozzo, Bogota newsroom, 571 610 7944))
